=== progress-and-report
     1	---
     2	title: "Export progress and the report"
     3	description: Follow an export as it writes, cancel it, read its finish report, and find out why one failed.
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	
     8	After you choose **Export…** on the export sheet, Frame Job asks where to save, then writes the file behind a progress sheet. When it's done, the sheet tells you what the file holds and what went wrong, if anything did.
     9	
    10	<AtAGlance
    11	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
    12	  keys="⌘E"
    13	  where="The Exporting sheet"
    14	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
    15	/>
    16	
    17	**Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then writes the file behind the editor so you can keep working. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
    18	
    19	## The save panel
    20	
    21	The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written:
    22	
    23	| Format | Message |
    24	| --- | --- |
    25	| A movie | "Export the timeline as a movie." |
    26	| Animated GIF | "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." |
    27	| Animated PNG | "Export the timeline as an animated APNG." |
    28	| Audio only | "Export the timeline's audio." |
    29	
    30	Cancelling the save panel writes nothing. The export sheet has already closed by then, and it keeps the choices you made for next time.
    31	
    32	## The Exporting sheet
    33	
    34	**Exporting** shows a progress bar, a percentage and a status line. The status line moves through these:
    35	
    36	| Status line | What's happening |
    37	| --- | --- |
    38	| "Preparing “*name*”…" | Frame Job is getting everything ready, and may be waiting for something the file needs. |
    39	| "Measuring loudness…" | The sound is being [measured](/export/loudness/#how-normalisation-works). Every export with sound does this, whether or not you chose a target. |
    40	| "Writing “*name*”…" | The file is being written. |
    41	
    42	The file is written from the timeline as it was when you confirmed it.
    43	
    44	### While it says Preparing
    45	
    46	An export never leaves out something that isn't ready, so it waits for these first:
    47	
    48	- The person and foreground masks of every [Remove Background](/export/what-an-export-includes/) clip in the range. This wait has no time limit. Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports wait for masks too.
    49	- Each clip's pointer, from its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
    50	- The measured loudness of every clip with a gate, leveller or de-esser, for up to five minutes.
    51	- The rendered sound of speed ramps, clips at another speed with Keep pitch off, [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).
    52	
    53	GIF and APNG files have no sound, so they don't wait for the last two. You can cancel during any of these waits.
    54	
    55	## Cancel a running export
    56	
    57	Choose **Cancel**. The status line reads "Stopping…" until the export has stopped, then the sheet closes and the half-written file is removed.
    58	
    59	:::caution
    60	If you chose to replace an existing file in the save panel, that file is gone once you cancel. Cancelling doesn't bring it back.
    61	:::
    62	
    63	## The finish report
    64	
    65	When an export finishes, the status line names the file and says what the sound measured:
    66	
    67	> Exported “name.mp4”. Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS.
    68	
    69	[What the loudness line means](/export/loudness/#what-the-loudness-line-means) explains those figures. A file with no sound has no figures. An export with [stems](/export/stems/) counts them after the name: "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems."
    70	
    71	**Show in Finder** reveals the file and closes the sheet. **Close** closes the sheet.
    72	
    73	## Graphic and cursor warnings
    74	
    75	A warning doesn't stop an export. The finish line adds a count, and its tooltip lists each warning.
    76	
    77	| Warning | What happened | What the tooltip lists |
    78	| --- | --- | --- |
    79	| "1 graphic warning (hover for details)." | A [graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) warned while the file was drawn. | Each warning, with the graphic's name and its frame. |
    80	| "1 cursor warning (hover for details)." | A clip's cursor file couldn't be drawn, so that clip is written without its pointer. | Each one, for example "The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …" |
    81	
    82	The cursor count comes after the graphic count. A finished row in the Export Queue shows the same counts, and its tooltip lists the same warnings.
    83	
    84	## Failures
    85	
    86	An export that can't run says why in a sentence, on the sheet or on its queue row. On the sheet, **Close** dismisses it.
    87	
    88	| The sheet says | What to do |
    89	| --- | --- |
    90	| "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first." | Add a clip. |
    91	| "The export was not started: the graphic …" | A graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module. Fix it and export again. |
    92	| "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic …" | A graphic failed at that frame. No file is left. |
    93	| "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser can't be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again. |
    94	| "Clip …'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | The sound of a speed change couldn't be made. |
    95	| "Clip …'s isolated voice could not be rendered: …" | Voice Isolation couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
    96	| "Clip …'s voice effect could not be rendered: …" | The voice effect couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
    97	| "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …" or "Clip …'s foreground masks could not be made: …" | A Remove Background clip's masks failed. No frame is written without them. |
    98	| "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose another format. No file is left. |
    99	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | A custom size has a different shape from the canvas. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
   100	
   101	Other messages come from macOS or the file being written, and appear as they are.
   102	
   103	A failure is different from a cancel. A failed Animated GIF, Animated PNG or WebM export removes its partly written file, and so does a failed export with stems. Any other format that fails while writing can leave a partly written file at the path you chose. It isn't a finished export, so delete it.
   104	
   105	## Quitting during an export
   106	
   107	Quitting while the Exporting sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel the export first.
   108	
   109	Only the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) is guarded at quit, so jobs there ask before they stop.
   110	
   111	## With an agent
   112	
   113	An agent's `export` puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, with no progress sheet. A bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline or a graphic that doesn't compile comes back from `export` before anything is queued. Failures while writing, the loudness figures and warnings come back from `export_status`, and `cancel_export` stops the job. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
   114

3	/// The export sheet's ANSWER half: read the controls, ask the core what they
4	/// describe, and repaint the card from what it said.
5	///
6	/// The seam is the §7 rule the sheet is built on, drawn as a file boundary.
7	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` owns the controls — it makes the popups and
8	/// the fields, lists the sizes, and hands a person something to choose with.
9	/// Nothing there decides an output size, a rate or a duration, because
10	/// nothing in this dialog does: every number the card shows comes back from
11	/// `rc_export_settings`, and this file is the whole of the round trip. It
12	/// turns a selection into the override object the core reads (`overrides()`),
13	/// sends it (`resolve()`), and writes the answer into the readout, the
14	/// footnote and the controls' enablement (`syncReadout()`). Between those
15	/// three, the `current…` accessors are the one place a popup index becomes a
16	/// meaning, so a control's index arithmetic is never spelled twice.
17	///
18	/// The one number the sheet DOES choose is the bit rate, and it is here for
19	/// that reason rather than beside the Quality popup: a tier is a REQUEST
20	/// (`ExportSheetOptions.swift` holds the ladder), and turning one into bits
21	/// per second needs the frame the controls are asking for — which is
22	/// `requestedFormat()`, three accessors deep into this file and nowhere near
23	/// the popup.
24	///
25	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
26	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
27	/// methods, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
28	/// visibility**, for the reason `ExporterLoudness.swift` records — `private`
29	/// on an extension member reaches only its own file, and a stored property
30	/// cannot live in an extension at all. So every control, every field and
31	/// every piece of state this file reads is internal in the file that
32	/// declares it, and the four members the controls call back into —
33	/// `resolve()`, `currentPreset`, `isCustomSize` and `isCustomLoudness` — are
34	/// internal here. Everything else below stays `private`, because a `private`
35	/// extension member is reachable from the rest of THIS file, and nothing
36	/// outside it has ever asked.
37	/// Phase 7 added the OTHER direction to this file, and it belongs here for the
38	/// same reason the first one does: `currentChoice` is a reading of the
39	/// controls, exactly as `overrides()` is, and `apply(_:)` is that reading run
40	/// backwards. Keeping the pair together is what makes a saved preset and the
41	/// remembered choice provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand —
42	/// there is one account of what a stored choice means, and both halves of it
43	/// are on one screen.
44	extension ExportSheetController {
45	
46	    // MARK: - Resolving
47	
48	    /// Asks the core for the settings the current controls describe, then
49	    /// repaints the readout from the answer.
50	    ///
51	    /// A refusal is not an error dialog: the message goes in the readout and
52	    /// Export greys out, so a bad override reads as "this combination is not
53	    /// available" rather than interrupting the person adjusting it.
54	    func resolve() {
55	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset else {
56	            resolved = nil
57	            resolveError = "This build has no export presets."
58	            syncReadout()
59	            return
60	        }
61	        // A format whose sizes the core could not list is not exported at
62	        // all, whatever the settings call would answer: the one refusal
63	        // `rc_export_sizes` shares with `rc_export_settings` is an unknown
64	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
65	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
66	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
67	        if let message = sizesError {
68	            resolved = nil
69	            resolveError = message
70	            syncReadout()
71	            return
72	        }
73	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
74	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
75	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
76	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
77	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
78	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
79	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
80	        {
81	            resolved = nil
82	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
83	            syncReadout()
84	            return
85	        }
86	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
87	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
88	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
89	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
90	            resolved = nil
91	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
92	            syncReadout()
93	            return
94	        }
95	        do {
96	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
97	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
98	            resolveError = nil
99	        } catch {
100	            resolved = nil
101	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
102	        }
103	        syncReadout()
104	    }
105	
106	    // MARK: - The card as a value
107	
108	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
109	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
110	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off
111	    /// an audio-only row carries no size, and one saved off a GIF carries no
112	    /// loudness — the record says what was actually asked for and never what
113	    /// a greyed-out popup happened to be sitting on.
114	    ///
115	    /// **The burn-in is gated by that same rule and used not to be**, which
116	    /// broke the sentence above rather than any of the core's: a tick made on
117	    /// an H.264 row and carried across to WAV was written into the record
118	    /// beside a size, an fps and a tier all three deliberately left empty, so
119	    /// a named preset — and the remembered choice, which is this same
120	    /// value — said a file with no picture would carry a burn-in. It is not an
121	    /// override, so nothing downstream ever refused it; `Applies.burnIn`
122	    /// (below) is where it is refused now.
123	    ///
124	    /// The `name` is empty: naming a choice is the Save… item's business.
125	    var currentChoice: ExportChoice {
126	        var choice = ExportChoice(presetID: currentPreset?.id ?? "")
127	        if currentApplies.size {
128	            if isCustomSize {
129	                choice.customSize = [clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField)]
130	            } else {
131	                let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
132	                // The ROW's id, never its index (`ExportChoice.sizeRow`).
133	                // Index 0 is recorded like any other: it is a row a person
134	                // chose, and `sizeOverride()`'s decision to send it as no
135	                // override at all is about the CORE's default and not about
136	                // what the popup was showing.
137	                if index >= 0, index < visibleSizes.count {
138	                    choice.sizeRow = visibleSizes[index].id
139	                }
140	            }
141	        }
142	        choice.fps = currentRate.map { [$0.num, $0.den] }
143	        choice.qualityTier = currentTier?.name
144	        choice.loudness = currentLoudness
145	        choice.inOutRange = rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1
146	        choice.burnInTimecode = currentApplies.burnIn && recipeOptions.burnInTimecode
147	        choice.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeedChoice.rawValue
148	        choice.audioBits = audioBitsChoice
149	        choice.stems = stemsChoice
150	        return choice
151	    }

153	    /// Writes a stored choice back into the controls. **The order is
154	    /// load-bearing and this method is where it is written down**; every
155	    /// caller — the remembered choice in `loadView`, a preset picked from the
156	    /// popup — goes through here so there is only ever one order.
157	    ///
158	    /// 1. **Format FIRST, before the sizes are listed.** A programmatic
159	    ///    `selectItem` sends no action, so `formatChanged`'s `sizesPreset`
160	    ///    guard never fires and nothing rebuilds on its own; listing after the
161	    ///    pick is what makes the rows this format's rows.
162	    /// 2. **Size AFTER `rebuildSizes()`**, which ends with an unconditional
163	    ///    `sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)` and would undo a selection made before
164	    ///    it.
165	    /// 3. **A custom LOUDNESS selects "Custom…" first and fills the field
166	    ///    second**, because `syncReadout` overwrites that field from the popup
167	    ///    whenever the popup is not on Custom — and `resolve()` runs one
168	    ///    `syncReadout` after this returns.
169	    /// 4. **`in_out` degrades to "Whole project"** on a document that has no
170	    ///    range: the popup only carries that row when `range != nil`, so
171	    ///    selecting index 1 would select nothing at all.
172	    ///
173	    /// It does NOT resolve. The caller does, once, after the last control has
174	    /// moved — a resolve per control would be six FFI round trips to paint one
175	    /// card.
176	    func apply(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
177	        if let index = presets.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == choice.presetID }) {
178	            formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
179	        }
180	        rebuildSizes()
181	        applySize(choice)
182	
183	        if let fps = choice.fps, fps.count == 2,
184	            let index = Self.rates.firstIndex(where: { $0.num == fps[0] && $0.den == fps[1] })
185	        {
186	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
187	        } else {
188	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
189	        }
190	
191	        if let name = choice.qualityTier,
192	            let index = Self.tiers.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == name })
193	        {
194	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
195	        } else {
196	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
197	        }
198	
199	        applyLoudness(choice)
200	        rangePopup.selectItem(at: choice.inOutRange && range != nil ? 1 : 0)
201	        burnInCheckbox.state = choice.burnInTimecode ? .on : .off
202	        applySpeed(choice)
203	        applyAudioBits(choice)
204	        applyStems(choice)
205	    }
206	
207	    /// Step 2, after the listing. A row whose id this format does not offer —
208	    /// a GIF's cap under H.264, or a row `visibleSizes` hid because an earlier
209	    /// row already has its numbers — falls back to the SAME NUMBERS under
210	    /// whatever row does show them, and only then to the format's default.
211	    /// Hiding is a tidiness of the popup's (`visibleSizes`), so a choice of
212	    /// "1080p" on a 1920 × 1080 document has to land on "Document size" rather
213	    /// than be dropped: it is the same export.
214	    private func applySize(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
215	        if let row = choice.sizeRow {
216	            if let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == row }) {
217	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
218	                return
219	            }
220	            if let hidden = sizes.first(where: { $0.id == row }),
221	                let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: {
222	                    $0.width == hidden.width && $0.height == hidden.height
223	                })
224	            {
225	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
226	                return
227	            }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        guard let custom = choice.customSize, custom.count == 2 else { return }
231	        // "Custom…" is the item after the last visible row.
232	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: visibleSizes.count)
233	        widthField.integerValue = custom[0]
234	        heightField.integerValue = custom[1]
235	    }
236	
237	    /// Step 3: the row first, the field second.
238	    private func applyLoudness(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
239	        guard let target = choice.loudness else {
240	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
241	            return
242	        }
243	        if let index = Self.loudnessTargets.firstIndex(of: target) {
244	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
245	            return
246	        }
247	        loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1)
248	        loudnessField.doubleValue = target
249	    }
250	
251	    var currentPreset: ExportPreset? {
252	        let index = formatPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
253	        guard index >= 0, index < presets.count else { return nil }
254	        return presets[index]
255	    }

257	    private var currentApplies: Applies { Applies(currentPreset) }
258	
259	    /// True while the Size popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen — which is
260	    /// also the state of a popup whose listing failed, since Custom is then
261	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before
262	    /// the fields are read.
263	    var isCustomSize: Bool { sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == visibleSizes.count }
264	
265	    /// The frame-rate override, or nil for "Project rate" — and always nil
266	    /// for a preset that has no frames, so a rate picked for a movie cannot
267	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
268	    private var currentRate: Fps? {
269	        let index = ratePopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
270	        guard currentApplies.frameRate, index >= 0, index < Self.rates.count else { return nil }
271	        return Self.rates[index]
272	    }
273	
274	    /// The quality tier, or nil for "Format default" — and, on the same
275	    /// rule, always nil for a preset that takes no bit rate.
276	    private var currentTier: QualityTier? {
277	        let index = qualityPopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
278	        guard currentApplies.quality, index >= 0, index < Self.tiers.count else { return nil }
279	        return Self.tiers[index]
280	    }
281	
282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.
283	    var isCustomLoudness: Bool {
284	        loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem == Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1
285	    }
286	
287	    /// The integrated target to normalise to, or nil for "Off" — index 0 of
288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
290	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }
300	        return min(
301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)
302	    }
303	
304	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
305	    ///
306	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
307	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
308	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
309	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
310	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
311	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
312	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
313	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
314	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
315	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
316	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
317	        if isCustomSize {
318	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
319	        }
320	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
321	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
322	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
323	    }
324	
325	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
326	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
327	    ///
328	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
329	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
330	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
331	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
332	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
333	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
334	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
335	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
336	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
337	        // size (`export.rs`).
338	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
339	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
340	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
341	            width = size.width
342	            height = size.height
343	        }
344	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
345	    }
346	
347	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
348	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
349	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
350	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
351	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
352	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
353	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        let applies = currentApplies
355	        let format = requestedFormat()
356	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
357	            overrides["width"] = size.width
358	            overrides["height"] = size.height
359	        }
360	        if let fps = currentRate {
361	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
362	        }
363	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
364	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
365	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
366	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
367	        // row has neither.
368	        if let tier = currentTier {
369	            if applies.videoBitrate {
370	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
371	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
372	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
373	            }
374	            if applies.audioBitrate {
375	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
376	            }
377	        }
378	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
379	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
380	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
381	        if let target = currentLoudness {
382	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
383	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
384	        }
385	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
386	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
387	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
388	        // in/out range, silently.
389	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
390	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
391	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
392	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
393	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
394	            overrides["range"] = [
395	                "start": range.start,
396	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
397	            ]
398	        }
399	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides
400	    }

402	    private func clampedSize(_ field: NSTextField) -> Int {
403	        min(max(field.integerValue, Self.sizeRange.lowerBound), Self.sizeRange.upperBound)
404	    }
405	
406	    /// Rewrites the readout, the footnote, the controls' enablement and the
407	    /// Export button from `resolved`. The size fields follow the core while
408	    /// a row of the Size popup owns the size, which is what makes "Custom…"
409	    /// readable: pick it and the fields already hold the numbers to edit.
410	    ///
411	    /// Enablement comes from the FORMAT rather than from `resolved`, so a
412	    /// refused resolve leaves the controls where they were instead of
413	    /// greying out the very one that has to be changed to fix it.
414	    private func syncReadout() {
415	        let applies = currentApplies
416	        let custom = isCustomSize
417	        // A popup whose listing failed holds nothing to choose, and the one
418	        // control that can put a size back is the Format popup, so the size
419	        // controls grey out with it — the exception to the rule in the doc
420	        // comment above, for the one refusal no size can fix.
421	        let listed = sizesError == nil
422	        sizePopup.isEnabled = applies.size && listed
423	        for field in [widthField, heightField] {
424	            field.isEnabled = applies.size && listed && custom
425	            field.textColor = field.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
426	        }
427	        ratePopup.isEnabled = applies.frameRate
428	        qualityPopup.isEnabled = applies.quality
429	        syncQualityTitles(applies)
430	        loudnessPopup.isEnabled = applies.loudness
431	        loudnessField.isEnabled = applies.loudness && isCustomLoudness
432	        loudnessField.textColor = loudnessField.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
433	        if !isCustomLoudness {
434	            // The field mirrors the row that is chosen, exactly as the size
435	            // fields mirror the core's answer, so picking "Custom…" starts
436	            // from the number that was in force a moment before. "Off" has no
437	            // number of its own, so it shows the first target — the one
438	            // Custom is most likely to be an adjustment of.
439	            loudnessField.doubleValue = currentLoudness ?? Self.loudnessTargets[0]
440	        }
441	        // The last control on the card, and the last one to be gated: the
442	        // burn-in stayed live on the three audio-only rows, alone among the
443	        // format-dependent controls, offering to write a timecode into a file
444	        // with no picture to write it into.
445	        burnInCheckbox.isEnabled = applies.burnIn
446	        syncDynamicRange(applies)
447	        syncSpeed(applies)
448	        syncAudioBits(applies)
449	        syncStems(applies)
450	
451	        guard let settings = resolved else {
452	            summaryLabel.stringValue = resolveError ?? "These settings are not available."
453	            summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
454	            footnote.stringValue = ""
455	            footnote.toolTip = nil
456	            exportButton?.isEnabled = false
457	            return
458	        }
459	        if !custom {
460	            widthField.integerValue = settings.width
461	            heightField.integerValue = settings.height
462	        }
463	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
464	        summaryLabel.stringValue = summary(for: settings)
465	        footnote.stringValue = footnoteText(for: settings)
466	        footnote.toolTip = footnote.stringValue
467	        exportButton?.isEnabled = settings.duration > 0
468	    }
469	
470	    /// Re-titles the tier rows with the rate each would ask for at the size
471	    /// and frame rate now chosen. "High" on its own says nothing; "High ·
472	    /// 8.0 Mbps" is the control's actual promise, and it has to move when
473	    /// the frame it is a rate for moves.
474	    private func syncQualityTitles(_ applies: Applies) {
475	        let format = requestedFormat()
476	        let codec = currentPreset?.codec ?? ""
477	        for (index, tier) in Self.tiers.enumerated() {
478	            guard let item = qualityPopup.item(at: index + 1) else { continue }
479	            if applies.videoBitrate {
480	                let rate = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
481	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps, codec: codec)
482	                let soft = applies.softCap ? "usually ≤ " : ""   // spec §11 CX-13
483	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(soft)\(Self.rateText(rate))"
484	            } else if applies.audioBitrate {
485	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(Self.rateText(tier.audioBitsPerSecond))"
486	            } else {
487	                item.title = tier.name
488	            }
489	        }
490	    }
491	
492	    /// The one-line description of what the file will contain.
493	    private func summary(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
494	        if settings.isAudioOnly {
495	            // Milliseconds rather than frames, and no rate in the line: audio
496	            // has no frames, which is the same reason the rate popup is
497	            // greyed out for this preset.
498	            let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: false)
499	            return "Audio only · \(duration)"
500	        }
501	        let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: true)
502	        var text = "\(settings.width) × \(settings.height) · \(settings.fps.displayName) fps · "
503	            + duration
504	        if Self.isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
505	            // What a GIF or an APNG costs is frames, not seconds — and it
506	            // carries no audio however much of it the timeline has, which is
507	            // worth saying before the export rather than after it.
508	            text += " · \(settings.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0) frames, no audio"
509	        }
510	        // A bundled encoder's estimate (spec §11 CX-18 (9)).
511	        if let line = ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: settings) { text += "\n" + line }
512	        return text
513	    }
514	
515	    /// The footnote over the buttons: the codec, the container, and the rates
516	    /// the CORE resolved — never the ones the tier asked for, and not filtered by
517	    /// what the sheet thinks applies, since a preset is free to carry a rate
518	    /// of its own that no control here offered.
519	    ///
520	    /// The distinction matters because `export.rs` drops override keys it
521	    /// does not know, silently (the same trap the range comment above names).
522	    /// A tier picked against a core that has no bit-rate overrides has to
523	    /// read as "the format's own rate" rather than let the popup imply a
524	    /// number the file will not have.
525	    private func footnoteText(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
526	        var parts = [settings.codec.uppercased()]
527	        let container = settings.container.uppercased()
528	        // A frame-sequence preset's codec IS its container: "GIF · GIF".
529	        if container != parts[0] { parts.append(container) }
530	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed { parts.append(speed.menuName) }
531	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { parts.append("24-bit") }
532	        if case let n = settings.stems.count, n > 0 { parts.append(n == 1 ? "1 stem" : "\(n) stems") }
533	        if let rate = settings.videoBitrate {
534	            // A bundled encoder's rate is a soft cap (spec §11 CX-13).
535	            parts.append((settings.writer == nil ? "" : "usually ≤ ") + Self.rateText(rate))
536	        }
537	        if let rate = settings.audioBitrate {
538	            parts.append("\(Self.rateText(rate)) audio")
539	        }
540	        if currentTier != nil, settings.videoBitrate == nil, settings.audioBitrate == nil {
541	            parts.append("format's own rate")
542	        }
543	        // The core's echo, not the popup's row: a build whose
544	        // `export_settings` has never heard of `loudness_lufs` drops the key
545	        // silently, and the footnote must not then promise a normalisation
546	        // the file will not have.
547	        if let target = settings.loudnessLufs {
548	            parts.append(
549	                String(format: "%g LUFS", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−"))
550	        }
551	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — the core's own
552	        // answer for this row (`ExportSettings.alpha`), never a reading of the
553	        // canvas. It is the one place the sheet says which format keeps a
554	        // transparent background, and it is a POSITIVE claim only: the rows
555	        // that answer false are not enumerated here, because the flag says
556	        // what the settings object says and the footnote's whole rule is that
557	        // it reports the core rather than the popup.
558	        if settings.alpha { parts.append("alpha") }
559	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")

3	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
4	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
5	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
6	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
7	/// take.
8	///
9	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
10	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
11	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
12	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
13	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
14	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
15	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
16	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
17	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
18	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
19	///
20	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
21	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
22	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
23	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
24	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
25	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
26	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
27	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
28	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
29	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
30	/// before it took the Preset row on.
31	extension ExportSheetController {
32	
33	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
34	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
35	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
36	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
37	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
38	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
39	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192
40	
41	    // MARK: - Loudness
42	
43	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
44	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
45	    ///
46	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
47	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
48	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
49	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
50	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
51	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
52	
53	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
54	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
55	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
56	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
57	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
58	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
59	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
60	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
61	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
62	
63	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
64	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
65	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
66	    ///
67	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
68	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
69	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
70	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
71	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
72	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
73	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
74	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
75	        switch target {
76	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
77	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"
78	        default: return "\(value) LUFS"
79	        }
80	    }
81	
82	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
83	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
84	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message
85	    /// back.
86	    static let loudnessRange: ClosedRange<Double> = -70...0
87	
88	    // MARK: - Quality
89	
90	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
91	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
92	    ///
93	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
94	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
95	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
96	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
97	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
98	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
99	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
100	    /// on both sides.
101	    ///
102	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
103	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
104	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
105	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
106	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
107	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
108	    struct QualityTier {
109	        let name: String
110	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
111	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
112	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
113	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
114	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
115	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
116	
117	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
118	        ///
119	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
120	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
121	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
122	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
123	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
124	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
125	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
126	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
127	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
128	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
129	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
130	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
131	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
132	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
133	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
134	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
135	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
136	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
137	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
138	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
139	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
140	        }
141	
142	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
143	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
144	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
145	        }
146	    }
147	
148	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
149	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
150	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
151	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
152	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
153	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
154	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
155	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
156	    ]
157	
158	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
159	    ///
160	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
161	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
162	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
163	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
164	    struct Applies {
165	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
166	
167	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
168	            self.preset = preset
169	        }
170	
171	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
172	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
173	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
174	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
175	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
176	        }
177	
178	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
179	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
180	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
181	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
182	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
183	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
184	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
185	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
186	        }
187	
188	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
189	
190	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
191	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
192	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
193	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
194	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
195	
196	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
197	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
198	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
199	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
200	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a
201	        /// delivery target matters most).
202	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
203	
204	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG
205	        /// project's HDR picture (spec §11 HD-14 (h)).
206	        var dynamicRange: Bool { preset?.carriesHDR ?? false }
207	
208	        /// The Speed popup is live only on a row whose bundled encoder has
209	        /// speeds (spec §11 CX-12 (2); not `vp9_webm`, CX-16 (2)).
210	        var encoderSpeed: Bool { !(preset?.encoderSpeeds.isEmpty ?? true) }
211	
212	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the
213	        /// uncompressed WAV and AIFF rows (spec §11 AU-29).
214	        var audioBits: Bool { !(preset?.audioBits.isEmpty ?? true) }
215	
216	        /// The Stems popup is live only on a row that lists modes: the three
217	        /// audio rows (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
218	        var stems: Bool { !(preset?.stems.isEmpty ?? true) }
219	
220	        /// The video rate is a soft cap on every row a bundled encoder writes
221	        /// (spec §11 CX-13, CX-16 (7)), whether or not it has speeds.
222	        var softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }
223	    }
224	
225	    /// GIF and APNG. Spelled once, and taken from the container rather than
226	    /// the codec because that is the field both `ExportPreset` and
227	    /// `ExportSettings` carry.
228	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
229	        let container = container.lowercased()
230	        return container == "gif" || container == "apng"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// A bit rate as the tier rows and the footnote spell it.
234	    static func rateText(_ bitsPerSecond: Int) -> String {
235	        if bitsPerSecond >= 1_000_000 {
236	            return String(format: "%.1f Mbps", Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1_000_000)
237	        }
238	        return "\(Int((Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1000).rounded())) kbps"
239	    }
240	}

3	/// The export sheet's SAVED PRESETS: the popup that lists them, the gear that
4	/// saves and deletes one, and the rule that a hand change to any control drops
5	/// the popup back to "Custom".
6	///
7	/// A fourth file for one card, and it is the same payment the other three
8	/// record: `ExportSheetController.swift` stood at the ~600-line cap and had to
9	/// give something up before it took this on. The seam is a clean one. The
10	/// controller BUILDS the card's controls and commits it; `Options` is what a
11	/// control means before any of them is read; `Resolve` turns a selection into
12	/// the core's answer and back; and this file owns the LIST — a thing that
13	/// outlives the sheet, lives in a file in Application Support, and is the only
14	/// part of the card with a store behind it. Nothing here computes an export
15	/// setting, and nothing here reads one.
16	///
17	/// What a preset IS lives next to the file that holds it
18	/// (`ExportPresetsStore.swift`), and applying one is `Resolve`'s `apply(_:)` —
19	/// the same method the remembered choice goes through, which is what makes a
20	/// saved preset provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand.
21	///
22	/// The toll is the split's usual one: `presetRow()`, `buildPresetMenuButton()`,
23	/// `presetEdited()` and `presetChanged(_:)` are internal because `loadView` and
24	/// the control actions in the controller call them, and every stored control
25	/// they touch was already internal for the same reason. `saveChoice` and
26	/// `deleteChoice` are internal for a different one, and it is the reason they
27	/// exist as a pair separate from the two gear items: the items run an app-modal
28	/// alert and a menu, neither of which a headless script can answer, so the two
29	/// WRITES sit under them where a probe compiled from `app/Sources` can drive
30	/// what the file actually does.
31	extension ExportSheetController {
32	
33	    /// The Preset popup and its gear, together on one row: 216 + 6 + 36 fits
34	    /// the 318 points the 480-wide card leaves beside its 106 label column.
35	    /// The card's width is the owner's (`cardWidth`, #243), not this row's:
36	    /// the row fitted the 420-wide card it was built on exactly.
37	    func presetRow() -> NSStackView {
38	        sheetRow([presetPopup, presetMenuButton])
39	    }
40	
41	    /// The gear: a pull-down, whose item 0 is its own face rather than a row.
42	    ///
43	    /// `autoenablesItems` stays ON and `validateMenuItem` answers for Delete.
44	    /// The pitfall recorded for the Remove Silences sheet is the same
45	    /// mechanism read the other way — a popup's menu validates its own rows,
46	    /// so an item disabled by hand is switched straight back on unless
47	    /// autoenabling is turned off first. Rather than turn it off and then
48	    /// re-synchronise Delete from four places, this uses the validation it
49	    /// would have been fighting.
50	    func buildPresetMenuButton() {
51	        let menu = NSMenu()
52	        let face = NSMenuItem()
53	        face.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "gearshape", accessibilityDescription: "Presets")?
54	            .withSymbolConfiguration(NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 11, weight: .regular))
55	        // A build with no SF Symbol still needs a face somebody can hit — and
56	        // the image-only position has to go with the image, or the fallback
57	        // draws nothing at all.
58	        if face.image == nil {
59	            face.title = "⋯"
60	        } else {
61	            presetMenuButton.imagePosition = .imageOnly
62	        }
63	        menu.addItem(face)
64	        for (title, action) in [
65	            ("Save…", #selector(savePreset(_:))), ("Delete", #selector(deletePreset(_:))),
66	        ] {
67	            let item = NSMenuItem(title: title, action: action, keyEquivalent: "")
68	            item.target = self
69	            menu.addItem(item)
70	        }
71	        presetMenuButton.menu = menu
72	        presetMenuButton.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 36).isActive = true
73	        // Icon-only, so the tooltip is the only thing that names it.
74	        presetMenuButton.toolTip = "Save these settings as a preset, or delete the chosen one"
75	    }
76	
77	    /// Refills the Preset popup from `userPresets` and selects `name`, or the
78	    /// "Custom" row when there is no such preset — which is also what a fresh
79	    /// sheet, a delete and any hand change to a control land on.
80	    func rebuildPresetPopup(selecting name: String?) {
81	        let menu = NSMenu()
82	        menu.addItem(NSMenuItem(title: Self.customPresetTitle, action: nil, keyEquivalent: ""))
83	        if !userPresets.presets.isEmpty {
84	            menu.addItem(.separator())
85	            for choice in userPresets.presets {
86	                let item = NSMenuItem(title: choice.name, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
87	                item.representedObject = choice
88	                menu.addItem(item)
89	            }
90	        }
91	        presetPopup.menu = menu
92	        if let name = name,
93	            let item = menu.items.first(where: {
94	                ($0.representedObject as? ExportChoice).map {
95	                    ExportPresetsStore.normalized($0.name) == ExportPresetsStore.normalized(name)
96	                } ?? false
97	            })
98	        {
99	            presetPopup.select(item)
100	        } else {
101	            presetPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
102	        }
103	    }
104	
105	    /// The popup's first row: not a preset, and the state of a card whose
106	    /// controls match none of them. `DocumentPane`'s Canvas popup spells the
107	    /// same case the same way, one tab away.
108	    static let customPresetTitle = "Custom"
109	
110	    /// The saved preset the popup is on, or nil for "Custom".

112	        presetPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? ExportChoice
113	    }

115	    // MARK: - Choosing, saving, deleting
116	
117	    /// Applies a saved preset, or does nothing at all for the "Custom" row.
118	    ///
119	    /// Nothing, and not a beep: "Custom" is reachable by moving any control,
120	    /// so picking it is a request to leave the card alone rather than one the
121	    /// sheet cannot honour. (`DocumentPane`'s Canvas popup beeps on the same
122	    /// row, because there picking Custom is a request for a size the popup
123	    /// has no way to supply.)
124	    @objc func presetChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
125	        guard let choice = selectedUserPreset else { return }
126	        apply(choice)
127	        resolveCard()
128	    }
129	
130	    /// Any hand change to a control drops the popup back to "Custom": the row
131	    /// names a set of choices, and once one of them has moved the card is no
132	    /// longer that preset.
133	    ///
134	    /// It does NOT compare the card against the preset — changing a value back
135	    /// does not re-arm the row. A comparison would have to answer whether a
136	    /// size row hidden as a duplicate of the document's own counts as the same
137	    /// choice (`visibleSizes`), and be wrong in one direction or the other;
138	    /// "you changed it" needs no such answer and is what every preset popup a
139	    /// person has met already does.
140	    func presetEdited() {
141	        if presetPopup.indexOfSelectedItem > 0 { presetPopup.selectItem(at: 0) }
142	    }

144	    /// Gear ▸ Save…. Names the card's current choices and writes them.
145	    @objc private func savePreset(_ sender: Any?) {
146	        // The same first-responder commit `exportClicked` makes, and for the
147	        // same reason: a typed custom size or loudness has not been committed
148	        // while its field editor still has it, so the choice read below would
149	        // be the one from before the edit. It is also what makes the guard
150	        // under it read the CURRENT card — ending the edit runs
151	        // `controlTextDidEndEditing`, which re-resolves.
152	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
153	        // **A card that cannot be exported cannot be named**, which is the
154	        // same fact `commit(queue:)` guards on one file over and the one
155	        // Export… is greyed out by. Without it Save… was the single
156	        // unguarded reader of `currentChoice`, and `currentChoice` has no
157	        // refusals in it: an empty Custom width reads through
158	        // `clampedSize` as the 16-pixel floor `resolve()` explicitly refuses
159	        // to export ("an export nobody asked for"), so the file got
160	        // `"custom_size": [16, 1080]` — a preset that applies cleanly,
161	        // resolves, and exports a 16-pixel movie from a card whose readout
162	        // said "Type a width and a height". The Custom LOUDNESS field has the
163	        // identical hole and this closes it too: `currentLoudness` answers nil
164	        // on an empty field, so the preset would have recorded Off while the
165	        // popup showed "Custom…".
166	        //
167	        // A beep and not a greyed-out row, deliberately: `validateMenuItem`
168	        // runs when the gear's menu OPENS, and a click on a button does not
169	        // end a field's edit (`commit(queue:)`'s own comment), so `resolved`
170	        // there can still describe the card from before the number now on
171	        // screen — it would grey out Save… on a card the person has just
172	        // fixed. Here, after the responder commit, the fact is current.
173	        guard resolved != nil else {
174	            NSSound.beep()
175	            return
176	        }
177	        guard let typed = askPresetName(suggesting: selectedUserPreset?.name ?? "") else { return }
178	        let name = ExportPresetsStore.normalized(typed)
179	        // The one name a preset may not take: it would read as the popup's
180	        // own first row, which is not a preset and cannot be deleted.
181	        guard !name.isEmpty,
182	            name.caseInsensitiveCompare(Self.customPresetTitle) != .orderedSame
183	        else {
184	            NSSound.beep()
185	            return
186	        }
187	        var choice = currentChoice
188	        choice.name = name
189	        guard saveChoice(choice) else {
190	            NSSound.beep()
191	            return
192	        }
193	        rebuildPresetPopup(selecting: name)
194	    }

196	    /// Gear ▸ Delete, on the preset the popup is showing.
197	    ///
198	    /// No confirmation, and that is a considered answer rather than an
199	    /// omission: deleting leaves every control exactly where the preset put

204	            NSSound.beep()
205	            return

208	    }

213	    /// whether the write landed, so the caller can beep.
214	    ///
215	    /// **The store is re-READ here rather than written from the snapshot the
216	    /// sheet opened with**, and that is the whole of these two methods.
217	    /// `userPresets` is loaded once per controller and a controller is built
218	    /// per ⌘E, so one window that opens, saves and closes is always current —
219	    /// but a sheet is WINDOW-modal, two documents can hold two cards at once
220	    /// (and two app instances one file), and `write()` replaces the file
221	    /// whole. Saving "Master" from a card whose snapshot predates the other
222	    /// window's "Web" would have written a file holding only "Master", with
223	    /// "Web" still listed in the popup that had just saved it — exactly the
224	    /// promise `savePreset` makes and cannot keep from a stale value. Reading
225	    /// first costs one small file read per Save… and brings the other
226	    /// window's additions into this popup for free.
227	    ///
228	    /// What re-reading cannot fix is the OTHER card's popup, which goes on
229	    /// listing a preset this one deleted until it is rebuilt. That is display
230	    /// staleness rather than loss: the store's promise is about the write, and
231	    /// this is what keeps the write honest.
232	    ///
233	    /// Written FIRST, and adopted only if the write landed, so the popup can
234	    /// never list a preset the file does not hold. Internal so a probe
235	    /// compiled from `app/Sources` can drive it: the action above runs an
236	    /// app-modal alert, which no headless script can answer.
237	    @discardableResult
238	    func saveChoice(_ choice: ExportChoice) -> Bool {
239	        let updated = ExportPresetsStore.load().saving(choice)
240	        guard updated.write() else { return false }
241	        userPresets = updated
242	        return true
243	    }
244	
245	    /// Removes one preset from disk and adopts the result, on the same terms:
246	    /// the file is re-read first, so a delete cannot take a preset another
247	    /// open card saved after this one's snapshot down with it.
248	    @discardableResult
249	    func deleteChoice(named name: String) -> Bool {
250	        let updated = ExportPresetsStore.load().removing(named: name)
251	        guard updated.write() else { return false }
252	        userPresets = updated
253	        return true
254	    }
255	
256	    /// The name prompt: an app-modal alert with a text field in it.
257	    ///
258	    /// An alert rather than a second sheet, because a sheet presented out of
259	    /// a sheet's own action is refused (the note
260	    /// `TranscribeSheetController.swift` carries), and app-modal rather than
261	    /// sheet-modal because the answer is needed HERE, in the middle of an
262	    /// action — `FFmpegRewrap.ask` is the house precedent for exactly that
263	    /// shape. The card stays visible behind it, which is the point: the
264	    /// choices being named are the ones on screen.
265	    private func askPresetName(suggesting suggestion: String) -> String? {
266	        let alert = NSAlert()
267	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
268	        alert.messageText = "Save these export settings as a preset"
269	        alert.informativeText =
270	            "A preset stores the choices on this card — format, size, frame rate, quality, "
271	            + "loudness, range and burn-in — not the numbers they resolve to. Saving under "
272	            + "a name that already exists replaces that preset, and “"
273	            + ExportSheetController.customPresetTitle
274	            + "” is the popup's own first row rather than a name a preset may take."
275	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
276	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
277	        field.placeholderString = "Preset name"
278	        alert.accessoryView = field
279	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Save")
280	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
281	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
282	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return nil }
283	        return field.stringValue
284	    }
285	}

3	/// The export sheet's CONTROL CHOICES as a value, and the two places they are
4	/// kept: the last one used (`UserDefaults`) and the named ones a person saves
5	/// (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json`).
6	///
7	/// **A stored preset is what the CONTROLS said, never what the core resolved,
8	/// and that is the whole design.** Road map 2's phase 7 asks for "a name →
9	/// overrides map … resolved by the core's `export_settings` like any
10	/// overrides, so the core never learns about them". The last clause stands and
11	/// is why this file has no `rc_*` call in it and needs none. The first cannot
12	/// be built, for two independent reasons:
13	///
14	/// 1. **The encoding is not an override.** `rc_export_settings` takes the
15	///    preset id as a separate ARGUMENT, and `export_overrides.rs` has no
16	///    `preset` key — it ignores a key it does not know, silently, on purpose —
17	///    so a map that carried the format would drop it and every preset would
18	///    resolve as H.264.
19	/// 2. **A resolved map cannot restore the sheet.** The Quality popup stores a
20	///    bits-per-pixel TIER and derives a bit rate at pick time from the frame
21	///    the controls are asking for; the Size popup stores a ROW ID
22	///    (`export_size.rs`'s vocabulary). Handed back
23	///    `{width: 1920, height: 1080, video_bitrate: 8000000}` the sheet cannot
24	///    tell "1080p + High" from "Custom 1920 × 1080 + a typed rate" — and
25	///    re-applying an absolute bit rate on a document of another size silently
26	///    changes what "High" meant, which is exactly what a tier expressed in
27	///    bits per PIXEL exists to prevent.
28	///
29	/// So a preset is the row of choices a person made, and applying one is the
30	/// same code path as picking each control by hand: `ExportSheetController`'s
31	/// `apply(_:)` writes the controls, `overrides()` turns them into the core's
32	/// object, and `rc_export_settings` answers. Nothing here computes a size, a
33	/// rate or a duration, which is the §7 rule the whole sheet is built on.
34	///
35	/// The consequence worth knowing, because it is a FEATURE: a preset saved on a
36	/// 1080p document and applied to a 4K one exports 4K at the tier's rate for
37	/// 4K. It remembers the request, not the answer.
38	struct ExportChoice: Codable, Equatable {
39	    /// The preset's name as the popup lists it. Empty for the remembered
40	    /// choice, which is nobody's preset and is never listed — the field is
41	    /// part of the record because the FILE's shape is a flat list of named
42	    /// choices, and splitting the type in two to keep one string out of one
43	    /// of its two homes would buy nothing.
44	    var name: String = ""
45	
46	    /// `ExportPreset.id` — the core's own vocabulary for the encoding
47	    /// (`export_table.rs`), so a row renamed in the table still restores.
48	    var presetID: String = ""
49	
50	    /// `ExportSize.id` — "document", "1080p", "preset"… — and never an
51	    /// INDEX. `visibleSizes` drops every row whose numbers an earlier row
52	    /// already has, so index 2 names a different size on a vertical document
53	    /// than on a landscape one; the id is stable across both.
54	    var sizeRow: String?
55	
56	    /// `[width, height]` when "Custom…" was chosen. Exclusive with
57	    /// `sizeRow` in practice, and if a hand-edited file carries both the row
58	    /// wins, because a row is a thing the sheet can select and a custom size
59	    /// is only reachable through it.
60	    var customSize: [Int]?
61	
62	    /// `[num, den]`, or nil for "Project rate" — the popup's first row, which
63	    /// is no override at all.
64	    var fps: [Int]?
65	
66	    /// `QualityTier.name` ("Low", "Medium", "High", "Maximum"), or nil for
67	    /// "Format default". The NAME and not the derived bit rate: see the type
68	    /// doc's second reason.
69	    var qualityTier: String?
70	
71	    /// The integrated loudness target in LUFS, or nil for "Off".
72	    ///
73	    /// The number rather than the popup ROW, though the contract allows
74	    /// either. Restoring picks the matching row when there is one and
75	    /// "Custom…" otherwise, so a target of −16 comes back as the −16 row even
76	    /// if it was typed into the Custom field. That is a difference in which
77	    /// control is lit and in nothing else: `overrides()` reads the same
78	    /// number out of either state, so the file that gets written is
79	    /// identical, and one number cannot disagree with itself the way a row
80	    /// plus a value can.
81	    var loudness: Double?
82	
83	    /// True for "In/out range". Degrades to "Whole project" on a document
84	    /// that has no range — the popup only carries that row when it does.
85	    var inOutRange: Bool = false
86	
87	    /// The burn-in checkbox. It is a RECIPE option rather than an export
88	    /// override (`RecipeOptions`), but from this sheet's side it is one more
89	    /// control, and a preset that remembered every choice but that one would
90	    /// be a preset that quietly stopped burning in.
91	    var burnInTimecode: Bool = false
92	
93	    /// The Speed popup's last word (`EncoderSpeed`, spec §11 CX-12 (2)), stored on every
94	    /// row so the popup keeps it across formats; only `av1` sends it.
95	    var encoderSpeed: String?
96	
97	    /// The Bit depth popup's last choice (16 or 24, spec §11 AU-29), stored on every row so
98	    /// the popup keeps it across formats; only `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` send it.
99	    var audioBits: Int?
100	
101	    /// The Stems popup's last word ("tracks" or "names", nil for None, spec §11 AU-108),
102	    /// stored on every row so the popup keeps it across formats; only the audio rows send it.
103	    var stems: String?
104	
105	    /// The file's spelling. Snake case because a person can open
106	    /// `ExportPresets.json` in an editor, and because `burn_in_timecode` is
107	    /// then the same string the core's recipe options use — one name for one
108	    /// idea, even across the FFI it never crosses.
109	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
110	        case name
111	        case presetID = "preset_id"
112	        case sizeRow = "size_row"
113	        case customSize = "custom_size"
114	        case fps
115	        case qualityTier = "quality_tier"
116	        case loudness
117	        case inOutRange = "in_out_range"
118	        case burnInTimecode = "burn_in_timecode"
119	        case encoderSpeed = "encoder_speed"
120	        case audioBits = "audio_bits"
121	        case stems
122	    }
123	
124	    init(
125	        name: String = "", presetID: String = "", sizeRow: String? = nil,
126	        customSize: [Int]? = nil, fps: [Int]? = nil, qualityTier: String? = nil,
127	        loudness: Double? = nil, inOutRange: Bool = false, burnInTimecode: Bool = false,
128	        encoderSpeed: String? = nil, audioBits: Int? = nil, stems: String? = nil
129	    ) {
130	        self.name = name
131	        self.presetID = presetID
132	        self.sizeRow = sizeRow
133	        self.customSize = customSize
134	        self.fps = fps
135	        self.qualityTier = qualityTier
136	        self.loudness = loudness
137	        self.inOutRange = inOutRange
138	        self.burnInTimecode = burnInTimecode
139	        self.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeed
140	        self.audioBits = audioBits
141	        self.stems = stems
142	    }
143	
144	    /// Every key optional, every absence a default.
145	    ///
146	    /// Written by hand rather than synthesized because the synthesized
147	    /// decoder THROWS on a missing non-optional, and this record is read from
148	    /// a file a person can edit and from a defaults value an older build
149	    /// wrote. One missing `burn_in_timecode` would otherwise fail the whole
150	    /// array's decode and take every other preset down with it — the shape of
151	    /// failure `load()` promises never to have.
152	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
153	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
154	        name = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .name)) ?? ""
155	        presetID = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .presetID)) ?? ""
156	        sizeRow = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .sizeRow)
157	        customSize = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .customSize)
158	        fps = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .fps)
159	        qualityTier = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .qualityTier)
160	        loudness = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Double.self, forKey: .loudness)
161	        inOutRange = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .inOutRange)) ?? false
162	        burnInTimecode = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .burnInTimecode)) ?? false
163	        encoderSpeed = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .encoderSpeed)
164	        audioBits = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .audioBits)
165	        stems = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .stems)
166	    }
167	}

169	// MARK: - The last choice
170	
171	extension ExportChoice {
172	    /// The `UserDefaults` key the sheet reopens from.
173	    ///
174	    /// ONE key holding the whole record as JSON, rather than nine keys. The
175	    /// record is already a value that has to survive as a unit — half a
176	    /// remembered choice (a format from today, a size from a build that spelled
177	    /// its rows differently) is a sheet that lies about what it will export —
178	    /// and one key is one thing for `tools/proof/harness/main.swift`'s
179	    /// `pinDefaults` to pin.
180	    static let rememberedKey = "FrameJobExportChoice"
181	
182	    /// The last choice the person actually EXPORTED with, or nil the first
183	    /// time. An empty string reads as nil, which is what lets the harness pin
184	    /// the key to "" and mean "nothing remembered".
185	    static var remembered: ExportChoice? {
186	        guard let text = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: rememberedKey),
187	            !text.isEmpty, let data = text.data(using: .utf8)
188	        else { return nil }
189	        return try? JSONDecoder().decode(ExportChoice.self, from: data)
190	    }
191	
192	    /// Records this choice as the one the sheet reopens on. Written when the
193	    /// export is CONFIRMED and never when the sheet is cancelled: a card
194	    /// somebody opened, fiddled with and dismissed is not a choice they made.
195	    /// The name is dropped, because the remembered choice is nobody's preset.
196	    func remember() {
197	        var choice = self
198	        choice.name = ""
199	        guard let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(choice),
200	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
201	        else { return }
202	        UserDefaults.standard.set(text, forKey: Self.rememberedKey)
203	    }
204	}
