3	/// The export sheet's CONTROL CHOICES as a value, and the two places they are
4	/// kept: the last one used (`UserDefaults`) and the named ones a person saves
5	/// (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json`).
6	///
7	/// **A stored preset is what the CONTROLS said, never what the core resolved,
8	/// and that is the whole design.** Road map 2's phase 7 asks for "a name →
9	/// overrides map … resolved by the core's `export_settings` like any
10	/// overrides, so the core never learns about them". The last clause stands and
11	/// is why this file has no `rc_*` call in it and needs none. The first cannot
12	/// be built, for two independent reasons:
13	///
14	/// 1. **The encoding is not an override.** `rc_export_settings` takes the
15	///    preset id as a separate ARGUMENT, and `export_overrides.rs` has no
16	///    `preset` key — it ignores a key it does not know, silently, on purpose —
17	///    so a map that carried the format would drop it and every preset would
18	///    resolve as H.264.
19	/// 2. **A resolved map cannot restore the sheet.** The Quality popup stores a
20	///    bits-per-pixel TIER and derives a bit rate at pick time from the frame
21	///    the controls are asking for; the Size popup stores a ROW ID
22	///    (`export_size.rs`'s vocabulary). Handed back
23	///    `{width: 1920, height: 1080, video_bitrate: 8000000}` the sheet cannot
24	///    tell "1080p + High" from "Custom 1920 × 1080 + a typed rate" — and
25	///    re-applying an absolute bit rate on a document of another size silently
26	///    changes what "High" meant, which is exactly what a tier expressed in
27	///    bits per PIXEL exists to prevent.
28	///
29	/// So a preset is the row of choices a person made, and applying one is the
30	/// same code path as picking each control by hand: `ExportSheetController`'s
31	/// `apply(_:)` writes the controls, `overrides()` turns them into the core's
32	/// object, and `rc_export_settings` answers. Nothing here computes a size, a
33	/// rate or a duration, which is the §7 rule the whole sheet is built on.
34	///
35	/// The consequence worth knowing, because it is a FEATURE: a preset saved on a
36	/// 1080p document and applied to a 4K one exports 4K at the tier's rate for
37	/// 4K. It remembers the request, not the answer.
38	struct ExportChoice: Codable, Equatable {
39	    /// The preset's name as the popup lists it. Empty for the remembered
40	    /// choice, which is nobody's preset and is never listed — the field is
41	    /// part of the record because the FILE's shape is a flat list of named
42	    /// choices, and splitting the type in two to keep one string out of one
43	    /// of its two homes would buy nothing.
44	    var name: String = ""
45	
46	    /// `ExportPreset.id` — the core's own vocabulary for the encoding
47	    /// (`export_table.rs`), so a row renamed in the table still restores.
48	    var presetID: String = ""
49	
50	    /// `ExportSize.id` — "document", "1080p", "preset"… — and never an
51	    /// INDEX. `visibleSizes` drops every row whose numbers an earlier row
52	    /// already has, so index 2 names a different size on a vertical document
53	    /// than on a landscape one; the id is stable across both.
54	    var sizeRow: String?
55	
56	    /// `[width, height]` when "Custom…" was chosen. Exclusive with
57	    /// `sizeRow` in practice, and if a hand-edited file carries both the row
58	    /// wins, because a row is a thing the sheet can select and a custom size
59	    /// is only reachable through it.
60	    var customSize: [Int]?
61	
62	    /// `[num, den]`, or nil for "Project rate" — the popup's first row, which
63	    /// is no override at all.
64	    var fps: [Int]?
65	
66	    /// `QualityTier.name` ("Low", "Medium", "High", "Maximum"), or nil for
67	    /// "Format default". The NAME and not the derived bit rate: see the type
68	    /// doc's second reason.
69	    var qualityTier: String?
70	
71	    /// The integrated loudness target in LUFS, or nil for "Off".
72	    ///
73	    /// The number rather than the popup ROW, though the contract allows
74	    /// either. Restoring picks the matching row when there is one and
75	    /// "Custom…" otherwise, so a target of −16 comes back as the −16 row even
76	    /// if it was typed into the Custom field. That is a difference in which
77	    /// control is lit and in nothing else: `overrides()` reads the same
78	    /// number out of either state, so the file that gets written is
79	    /// identical, and one number cannot disagree with itself the way a row
80	    /// plus a value can.
81	    var loudness: Double?
82	
83	    /// True for "In/out range". Degrades to "Whole project" on a document
84	    /// that has no range — the popup only carries that row when it does.
85	    var inOutRange: Bool = false
86	
87	    /// The burn-in checkbox. It is a RECIPE option rather than an export
88	    /// override (`RecipeOptions`), but from this sheet's side it is one more
89	    /// control, and a preset that remembered every choice but that one would
90	    /// be a preset that quietly stopped burning in.
91	    var burnInTimecode: Bool = false
92	
93	    /// The Speed popup's last word (`EncoderSpeed`, spec §11 CX-12 (2)), stored on every
94	    /// row so the popup keeps it across formats; only `av1` sends it.
95	    var encoderSpeed: String?
96	
97	    /// The Bit depth popup's last choice (16 or 24, spec §11 AU-29), stored on every row so
98	    /// the popup keeps it across formats; only `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` send it.
99	    var audioBits: Int?
100	
101	    /// The Stems popup's last word ("tracks" or "names", nil for None, spec §11 AU-108),
102	    /// stored on every row so the popup keeps it across formats; only the audio rows send it.
103	    var stems: String?
104	
105	    /// The file's spelling. Snake case because a person can open
106	    /// `ExportPresets.json` in an editor, and because `burn_in_timecode` is
107	    /// then the same string the core's recipe options use — one name for one
108	    /// idea, even across the FFI it never crosses.
109	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
110	        case name
111	        case presetID = "preset_id"
112	        case sizeRow = "size_row"
113	        case customSize = "custom_size"
114	        case fps
115	        case qualityTier = "quality_tier"
116	        case loudness
117	        case inOutRange = "in_out_range"
118	        case burnInTimecode = "burn_in_timecode"
119	        case encoderSpeed = "encoder_speed"
120	        case audioBits = "audio_bits"
121	        case stems
122	    }
123	
124	    init(
125	        name: String = "", presetID: String = "", sizeRow: String? = nil,
126	        customSize: [Int]? = nil, fps: [Int]? = nil, qualityTier: String? = nil,
127	        loudness: Double? = nil, inOutRange: Bool = false, burnInTimecode: Bool = false,
128	        encoderSpeed: String? = nil, audioBits: Int? = nil, stems: String? = nil
129	    ) {
130	        self.name = name
131	        self.presetID = presetID
132	        self.sizeRow = sizeRow
133	        self.customSize = customSize
134	        self.fps = fps
135	        self.qualityTier = qualityTier
136	        self.loudness = loudness
137	        self.inOutRange = inOutRange
138	        self.burnInTimecode = burnInTimecode
139	        self.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeed
140	        self.audioBits = audioBits
141	        self.stems = stems
142	    }
143	
144	    /// Every key optional, every absence a default.
145	    ///
146	    /// Written by hand rather than synthesized because the synthesized
147	    /// decoder THROWS on a missing non-optional, and this record is read from
148	    /// a file a person can edit and from a defaults value an older build
149	    /// wrote. One missing `burn_in_timecode` would otherwise fail the whole
150	    /// array's decode and take every other preset down with it — the shape of
151	    /// failure `load()` promises never to have.
152	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
153	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
154	        name = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .name)) ?? ""
155	        presetID = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .presetID)) ?? ""
156	        sizeRow = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .sizeRow)
157	        customSize = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .customSize)
158	        fps = try? c.decodeIfPresent([Int].self, forKey: .fps)
159	        qualityTier = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .qualityTier)
160	        loudness = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Double.self, forKey: .loudness)
161	        inOutRange = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .inOutRange)) ?? false
162	        burnInTimecode = (try? c.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .burnInTimecode)) ?? false
163	        encoderSpeed = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .encoderSpeed)
164	        audioBits = try? c.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .audioBits)
165	        stems = try? c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .stems)
166	    }
167	}
168	
169	// MARK: - The last choice
170	
171	extension ExportChoice {
172	    /// The `UserDefaults` key the sheet reopens from.
173	    ///
174	    /// ONE key holding the whole record as JSON, rather than nine keys. The
175	    /// record is already a value that has to survive as a unit — half a
176	    /// remembered choice (a format from today, a size from a build that spelled
177	    /// its rows differently) is a sheet that lies about what it will export —
178	    /// and one key is one thing for `tools/proof/harness/main.swift`'s
179	    /// `pinDefaults` to pin.
180	    static let rememberedKey = "FrameJobExportChoice"
181	
182	    /// The last choice the person actually EXPORTED with, or nil the first
183	    /// time. An empty string reads as nil, which is what lets the harness pin
184	    /// the key to "" and mean "nothing remembered".
185	    static var remembered: ExportChoice? {
186	        guard let text = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: rememberedKey),
187	            !text.isEmpty, let data = text.data(using: .utf8)
188	        else { return nil }
189	        return try? JSONDecoder().decode(ExportChoice.self, from: data)
190	    }
191	
192	    /// Records this choice as the one the sheet reopens on. Written when the
193	    /// export is CONFIRMED and never when the sheet is cancelled: a card
194	    /// somebody opened, fiddled with and dismissed is not a choice they made.
195	    /// The name is dropped, because the remembered choice is nobody's preset.
196	    func remember() {
197	        var choice = self
198	        choice.name = ""
199	        guard let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(choice),
200	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
201	        else { return }
202	        UserDefaults.standard.set(text, forKey: Self.rememberedKey)
203	    }
204	}
205	
206	// MARK: - The named presets
207	
208	/// The named export presets, as a value: read the file, ask it questions, hand
209	/// back a NEW store with one more or one fewer, write it out.
210	///
211	/// `AudioNormalize.swift`'s shape applied to a preferences file — peaks in, ops
212	/// out; here, a file in, a list out — and for the same reason: the sheet's
213	/// Save… button and any later caller (the export queue, an agent) provably do
214	/// the same thing to the same list, because there is one implementation of what
215	/// "saving a preset" means and it has no `NSPopUpButton` in it.
216	///
217	/// **Every failure degrades to "no presets".** A missing file, a directory
218	/// where the file should be, a truncated write, a JSON object where an array
219	/// belongs, a record from a newer build: all of them answer an empty store, and
220	/// none of them throws, alerts or interrupts. The list is a convenience over a
221	/// dialog that works perfectly without it, so the worst outcome a corrupt file
222	/// may cause is that the popup is empty — never a lost export, never a crash,
223	/// and never a modal about a preferences file in the middle of somebody's work.
224	struct ExportPresetsStore: Equatable {
225	    /// The file inside `AppSupport.directory`.
226	    static let fileName = "ExportPresets.json"
227	
228	    /// In the order they were first saved. Not sorted: a person's own order is
229	    /// information, and re-saving under an existing name REPLACES that record
230	    /// in place rather than moving it to the end, so the popup does not
231	    /// reshuffle under the pointer.
232	    private(set) var presets: [ExportChoice] = []
233	
234	    static var url: URL? { AppSupport.file(fileName) }
235	
236	    /// The store on disk, or an empty one. See the type doc: there is no
237	    /// failing path out of this.
238	    static func load() -> ExportPresetsStore {
239	        guard let url = url, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
240	            let decoded = try? JSONDecoder().decode([ExportChoice].self, from: data)
241	        else { return ExportPresetsStore() }
242	        var store = ExportPresetsStore()
243	        // A record with no name cannot be listed (the popup is keyed by
244	        // title) and cannot be deleted, so it is dropped rather than shown as
245	        // a blank row. A hand-edited file is the only way to make one.
246	        store.presets = decoded.filter { !Self.normalized($0.name).isEmpty }
247	        return store
248	    }
249	
250	    /// Names compare TRIMMED and case-insensitively, which is the whole of the
251	    /// uniqueness rule. Two presets may not share a name — `NSPopUpButton`
252	    /// aside (its `addItem(withTitle:)` silently REMOVES an existing row with
253	    /// the same title, which is why the sheet builds its menu out of
254	    /// `NSMenuItem`s instead), two rows a person reads as identical are two
255	    /// rows they cannot choose between, and Delete would have to guess which
256	    /// one they meant.
257	    static func normalized(_ name: String) -> String {
258	        name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
259	    }
260	
261	    private static func matches(_ a: String, _ b: String) -> Bool {
262	        normalized(a).caseInsensitiveCompare(normalized(b)) == .orderedSame
263	    }
264	
265	    func preset(named name: String) -> ExportChoice? {
266	        presets.first { Self.matches($0.name, name) }
267	    }
268	
269	    /// A store with `choice` in it, under its own (trimmed) name.
270	    ///
271	    /// An existing name is REPLACED in place — the same name means the same
272	    /// preset, so saving over one is an update and not a second row. The sheet
273	    /// says so before it asks; this is where it is true.
274	    func saving(_ choice: ExportChoice) -> ExportPresetsStore {
275	        var stored = choice
276	        stored.name = Self.normalized(choice.name)
277	        guard !stored.name.isEmpty else { return self }
278	        var store = self
279	        if let index = store.presets.firstIndex(where: { Self.matches($0.name, stored.name) }) {
280	            store.presets[index] = stored
281	        } else {
282	            store.presets.append(stored)
283	        }
284	        return store
285	    }
286	
287	    func removing(named name: String) -> ExportPresetsStore {
288	        var store = self
289	        store.presets.removeAll { Self.matches($0.name, name) }
290	        return store
291	    }
292	
293	    /// Writes the list, creating `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` at
294	    /// `0700` (`AppSupport.ensureDirectory`) if this is the first thing to
295	    /// need it. Answers whether it landed, so a caller can beep; it never
296	    /// throws, for the reason the type doc gives.
297	    @discardableResult
298	    func write() -> Bool {
299	        guard let url = Self.url, let directory = AppSupport.directory else { return false }
300	        guard (try? AppSupport.ensureDirectory(directory)) != nil else { return false }
301	        let encoder = JSONEncoder()
302	        // Sorted keys and an indent so the file is diffable and readable by
303	        // the person whose Library it is in — it is a preferences file, not a
304	        // wire format, and nothing reads it hot.
305	        encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]
306	        guard let data = try? encoder.encode(presets) else { return false }
307	        return (try? data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)) != nil
308	    }
309	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

     8	/// is remembered with the rest of the card (`ExportChoice`).

     4	/// The export card's two commits, Export… and Add to Queue, which end in a save panel and hand
     5	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
     6	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
     7	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
     8	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).
     9	extension ExportSheetController {
    10	    // MARK: - Commit
    11	
    12	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    13	        dismiss(self)
    14	    }
    15	
    16	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
    17	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    18	        commit(queue: false)
    19	    }
    20	
    21	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
    22	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
    23	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    24	        commit(queue: true)
    25	    }
    26	
    27	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
    28	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
    29	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
    30	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
    31	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
    32	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
    33	    /// one held until its turn.
    34	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
    35	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
    36	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
    37	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
    38	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
    39	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
    40	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
    41	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
    42	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
    43	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
    44	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
    45	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
    46	              let window = editor.view.window
    47	        else {
    48	            NSSound.beep()
    49	            return
    50	        }
    51	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
    52	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
    53	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
    54	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
    55	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
    56	        let options = recipeOptions
    57	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
    58	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
    59	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
    60	        // buttons record it.
    61	        currentChoice.remember()
    62	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
    63	        dismiss(self)
    64	
    65	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
    66	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
    67	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
    68	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
    69	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
    70	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
    71	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
    72	        }
    73	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
    74	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
    75	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
    76	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }
    77	            // The handoff, and the only place the two buttons differ. The
    78	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
    79	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
    80	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
    81	            if queue {
    82	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
    83	            } else {
    84	                editor.beginExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
    85	            }
    86	        }
    87	    }
    88	
    89	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
    90	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
    91	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
    92	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
    93	    }

    10	//!   pictures, or nothing, is not) and it is not `silenced` among the

    12	//! - **Grouping.** `tracks`: one stem per heard track. `names`: heard tracks
    13	//!   whose trimmed names match case-insensitively are one stem, named by the
    14	//!   first's spelling; an unnamed track is its own.
    15	//! - **Order.** Timeline order of each stem's first track; a stem's tracks

    17	//! - **Names.** The trimmed track name, else `Track N` (N = its index + 1,
    18	//!   the header's label), with `/` and `:` replaced by `-`; a name equal
    19	//!   case-insensitively to an earlier stem's gets ` (Track N)` of its first
    20	//!   track, and one still equal to an earlier stem's then gets
    21	//!   ` (Track N, 2)`, ` (Track N, 3)` and on, the first no earlier stem
    22	//!   holds, so no two stems share a file.

    40	impl Stem {
    41	    /// `{"name": …, "tracks": [ids]}`, the settings' `stems` entry.
    42	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {

    44	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name.clone()));
    45	        let tracks = self.tracks.iter().map(|id| Value::from(*id)).collect();

    51	/// A group while it is being gathered: its first track's index and the
    52	/// spelling it is named by.
    53	struct Group {
    54	    first: usize,
    55	    spelling: String,
    56	    tracks: Vec<u32>,
    57	}
    58	
    59	impl Project {
    60	    /// The stems `mode` asks for, in order (spec §11 AU-108 (b), (c)), or
    61	    /// the refusal when no track is heard.
    62	    pub(crate) fn export_stems(&self, mode: StemsMode) -> Result<Vec<Stem>, String> {
    63	        let labelled: BTreeSet<u32> = self.assign().audio.iter().map(|t| t.track).collect();
    64	        let mut groups: Vec<Group> = Vec::new();
    65	        for (index, track) in self.tracks.iter().enumerate() {
    66	            if !labelled.contains(&track.id) || silenced(&self.tracks, track) {
    67	                continue;
    68	            }
    69	            let trimmed = track.name.trim();
    70	            let joins = match mode {
    71	                StemsMode::Tracks => None,
    72	                StemsMode::Names if trimmed.is_empty() => None,
    73	                StemsMode::Names => groups
    74	                    .iter_mut()
    75	                    .find(|g| !g.spelling.is_empty() && same(&g.spelling, trimmed)),
    76	            };
    77	            match joins {
    78	                Some(group) => group.tracks.push(track.id),
    79	                None => groups.push(Group {
    80	                    first: index,
    81	                    spelling: trimmed.to_string(),
    82	                    tracks: vec![track.id],
    83	                }),
    84	            }
    85	        }
    86	        if groups.is_empty() {
    87	            return Err("stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".to_string());
    88	        }
    89	        let mut stems: Vec<Stem> = Vec::with_capacity(groups.len());
    90	        for group in groups {
    91	            let label = format!("Track {}", group.first.saturating_add(1));
    92	            let base = if group.spelling.is_empty() {
    93	                label.clone()
    94	            } else {
    95	                group.spelling.replace(['/', ':'], "-")
    96	            };
    97	            let taken = |name: &str| stems.iter().any(|s| same(&s.name, name));
    98	            let mut name = base.clone();
    99	            if taken(&name) {
   100	                name = format!("{base} ({label})");
   101	            }
   102	            let mut count: u32 = 2;
   103	            while taken(&name) {
   104	                name = format!("{base} ({label}, {count})");
   105	                count = count.saturating_add(1);
   106	            }
   107	            stems.push(Stem {
   108	                name,
   109	                tracks: group.tracks,
   110	            });
   111	        }
   112	        Ok(stems)
   113	    }
   114	}

     3	// The arithmetic that turns a loudness measurement into an export gain: a pure move out of
     4	// `Loudness.swift` (road map "audio" AP0's toll T3), which keeps the BS.1770-4 meter and the
     5	// `LoudnessReport` it answers.
     6	
     7	// MARK: - What an export did about it
     8	
     9	/// A measurement, the target it was measured against, and the gain that
    10	/// follows — the value both consumers of an export read (the progress
    11	/// sheet's final line and the `export` tool's result).
    12	///
    13	/// **The gain is applied under a master limiter** (spec §11 AU-27, AU-28):
    14	/// every export with sound runs `ExportAudioMaster` — the gain, then
    15	/// `AudioLimiterStage` at the export's ceiling — so the gain that reaches a
    16	/// target is solved through `AudioLimiterModel` over pass one's 10 ms steps,
    17	/// the model the clip limiter's Normalize already uses (AU-24). A scalar gain
    18	/// shifts the true peak by itself, and the master holds what passes the
    19	/// ceiling there, so the file's true peak is `min(measured + gain, ceiling)`
    20	/// and what the master took off is `limitedDB`. Nothing clips any more.
    21	///
    22	/// This file stays free of AVFoundation and AppKit: `phase5_chrome.py` §9
    23	/// compiles it with `Loudness.swift`, `StepLoudness.swift` and
    24	/// `AudioLimiterModel.swift` alone.
    25	struct ExportLoudness: Equatable {
    26	    /// What the mix measured, before any gain.
    27	    let measured: LoudnessReport
    28	    /// The integrated target that was asked for, or nil when the export was
    29	    /// not normalised at all and this is a readout.
    30	    let target: Double?
    31	    /// The master limiter's true-peak ceiling, dBTP.
    32	    let ceiling: Double
    33	    /// The gain that was applied, in dB. Quantised (see `gainStepDB`), and
    34	    /// exactly 0 when nothing was applied.
    35	    let gainDB: Double
    36	    /// What the file holds, LUFS: the model's figure at `gainDB` under the
    37	    /// master (AU-28), else the measurement shifted by the gain; nil when
    38	    /// gated out.
    39	    let integratedLUFS: Double?
    40	    /// True when the +40 dB cap, not the target, decided the gain — the case
    41	    /// worth reporting, because the file will then be quieter than asked.
    42	    let cappedByGain: Bool
    43	
    44	    /// The master's ceiling when a caller names none: AU-4's −1 dBTP, for
    45	    /// normalised and un-normalised exports alike (AU-27).
    46	    static let defaultCeiling: Double = -1
    47	
    48	    /// The most gain a target may ask for, dB.
    49	    static let maxGainDB: Double = 40
    50	
    51	    /// The master limiter's release, seconds (AU-27): `ExportAudioMaster`'s,
    52	    /// spelled here so the model and the stage read one number.
    53	    static let masterReleaseSeconds = 0.1
    54	
    55	    /// The fewest 10 ms steps the model is run over: one 400 ms gating block.
    56	    private static let modelSteps = 40
    57	
    58	    /// The grid the applied gain is rounded to, in dB — to NEAREST (AU-28):
    59	    /// the limiter holds the ceiling, so no rounding has to lean toward it.
    60	    ///
    61	    /// Not cosmetic. AVFoundation's mix is not bit-deterministic near a duck
    62	    /// ramp edge (CLAUDE.md records 38 samples of one 16-bit LSB), which
    63	    /// moves the measured loudness by something like 10⁻⁵ LU — irrelevant to
    64	    /// a ±0.5 LU target, but enough that a raw `Double` gain would differ in
    65	    /// its last bits between two runs and round the ENTIRE file's samples
    66	    /// differently. At 0.01 dB the two runs pick the same gain, so two
    67	    /// normalised exports of one project compare, and "−14.0 LUFS"
    68	    /// reproduces.
    69	    static let gainStepDB: Double = 0.01
    70	
    71	    /// The linear multiplier the master applies to the float mix.
    72	    var linearGain: Double { pow(10, gainDB / 20) }
    73	
    74	    /// True when the master has no gain to apply. It still limits and
    75	    /// quantises.
    76	    var isUnity: Bool { gainDB == 0 }
    77	
    78	    /// The file's true peak: the measurement shifted by the gain, held at the
    79	    /// ceiling. A non-finite measurement passes through unclamped, so the
    80	    /// summary can still say "Silent" (−∞) or that the peak could not be
    81	    /// measured (+∞).
    82	    var truePeakDBTP: Double {
    83	        guard measured.truePeakDBTP.isFinite else { return measured.truePeakDBTP }
    84	        return min(measured.truePeakDBTP + gainDB, ceiling)
    85	    }
    86	
    87	    /// How far the master turned the hottest peak down, dB: the shifted
    88	    /// measurement's excess over the ceiling, 0 when under it or not finite.
    89	    var limitedDB: Double {
    90	        guard measured.truePeakDBTP.isFinite else { return 0 }
    91	        return max(0, measured.truePeakDBTP + gainDB - ceiling)
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    /// The gain a `target` asks for over `measured` and its 10 ms `steps`
    95	    /// (energies) and `peaks` (true peaks, linear) under the master's
    96	    /// `ceiling` (spec §11 AU-28).
    97	    ///
    98	    /// `target` nil is "do not normalise": the measurement is still carried,
    99	    /// and the file's loudness is still the model's, because the master
   100	    /// limits an un-normalised mix that passes the ceiling too.
   101	    ///
   102	    /// A peak that is not a finite number keeps the old handling: no model,
   103	    /// no gain, the measured loudness. −∞ is digital silence; +∞ is float
   104	    /// source media holding a non-finite sample, and "the peak cannot be
   105	    /// measured" has to mean "do not push it up".
   106	    static func resolve(
   107	        measured: LoudnessReport, steps: [Double], peaks: [Double], target: Double?,
   108	        ceiling: Double?
   109	    ) -> ExportLoudness {
   110	        let ceiling = ceiling ?? defaultCeiling
   111	        guard measured.truePeakDBTP.isFinite else {
   112	            return ExportLoudness(
   113	                measured: measured, target: target, ceiling: ceiling, gainDB: 0,
   114	                integratedLUFS: measured.integratedLUFS, cappedByGain: false)
   115	        }
   116	        let linearCeiling = pow(10, ceiling / 20)
   117	        let modelled = steps.count >= modelSteps && StepLoudness.integrated(steps) != nil
   118	        var gainDB = 0.0
   119	        var capped = false
   120	        if let target, let integrated = measured.integratedLUFS {
   121	            let wanted: Double
   122	            if modelled {
   123	                let maxGain = pow(10, maxGainDB / 20)
   124	                let gain = AudioLimiterModel.gain(
   125	                    reaching: target, steps: steps, peaks: peaks, ceiling: linearCeiling,
   126	                    releaseSeconds: masterReleaseSeconds, maxGain: maxGain)
   127	                capped = gain >= maxGain
   128	                wanted = 20 * log10(gain)
   129	            } else {
   130	                // Under one gating block, or no float read: the unlimited gain.
   131	                wanted = target - integrated
   132	                capped = wanted > maxGainDB
   133	            }
   134	            let rounded = min((wanted / gainStepDB).rounded() * gainStepDB, maxGainDB)
   135	            gainDB = rounded.isFinite ? rounded : 0
   136	        }
   137	        let shifted = measured.integratedLUFS.map { $0 + gainDB }
   138	        let lufs = modelled
   139	            ? AudioLimiterModel.integrated(
   140	                steps: steps, peaks: peaks, gain: pow(10, gainDB / 20), ceiling: linearCeiling,
   141	                releaseSeconds: masterReleaseSeconds) ?? shifted
   142	            : shifted
   143	        return ExportLoudness(
   144	            measured: measured, target: target, ceiling: ceiling, gainDB: gainDB,
   145	            integratedLUFS: lufs, cappedByGain: capped)
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    /// The one line every export reports: `"Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS"`, with
   149	    /// `" · peaks limited by 8.6 dB"` when the master took 0.05 dB or more off.
   150	    var summary: String {
   151	        guard truePeakDBTP.isFinite else {
   152	            // −∞ is digital silence. Anything else non-finite is a mix
   153	            // carrying a non-finite sample, and calling THAT silent is the
   154	            // loudest lie this line could tell.
   155	            return truePeakDBTP == -.infinity
   156	                ? "Silent" : "Peak not measurable (a non-finite sample in the mix)"
   157	        }
   158	        let peak = "Peak \(Self.decibels(truePeakDBTP)) dBTP"
   159	        var measurement: String
   160	        if let integrated = integratedLUFS {
   161	            measurement = "\(peak) · \(Self.decibels(integrated)) LUFS"
   162	        } else {
   163	            // A programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose
   164	            // every block fell under Γa. It has a peak and no loudness, and
   165	            // saying which is better than printing −∞.
   166	            measurement = "\(peak) · loudness not measurable"
   167	        }
   168	        if limitedDB >= 0.05 {
   169	            measurement += " · peaks limited by \(Self.decibels(limitedDB)) dB"
   170	        }
   171	        return measurement
   172	    }
   173	
   174	    /// One decimal, with the typographic minus the rest of the chrome uses.
   175	    private static func decibels(_ value: Double) -> String {
   176	        String(format: "%.1f", value).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
   177	    }
   178	}

     3	/// Pass one of an export: read the composed mix and MEASURE it (`Loudness.swift`).
     4	///
     5	/// This is `Exporter`'s own "Measuring the mix" section, in a file of its own

     7	/// 5 put a second pass in it. It is a MOVE and nothing else — the same methods,

    10	/// `isCancelled` / `setMeasureProgress` accessors over that lock) are internal
    11	/// only to be reachable from here. Stored properties cannot live in an
    12	/// extension, which is the whole reason the split is where it is.
    13	///

    15	/// "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS" on its final line, and an export that asked to
    16	/// be normalised gets the gain that lands it on its target. The pass is a

    20	/// the number matters most.

    22	/// **It builds its OWN composition.** An `AVAudioMix` copy shares the

    26	/// them strictly in sequence would *probably* survive on `AudioTapContext`'s

    11	        /// by an empty timeline AND by one holding only text, shapes and

    13	        /// message has to name the second case, which is the surprising one.

    16	        /// unknown codec name, one `AVAssetWriter` refuses an input for, or
    17	        /// one whose encoder is not found when the write starts

    22	        /// type.

    25	        /// from the canvas, which cannot be written correctly and so is not
    26	        /// written at all (road map 2, phase 7b). Carries the canvas and the
    27	        /// size the core resolved, in that order.
    28	        ///
    29	        /// **Which sizes reach it** (spec §11 G-33 (c)): on `prores_4444` and
    30	        /// `hevc_alpha`, a frame more than a pixel off the canvas's shape
    31	        /// (`ExportWriter.shapeGap`: `gap > limit`). A frame within a pixel is
    32	        /// filled instead of padded and is written — the evened Document row
    33	        /// on a canvas with an odd edge, a standard row whose long edge
    34	        /// rounded, a size typed in the canvas's own proportions (evened
    35	        /// first on `hevc_alpha`, so an odd one is written a pixel smaller),
    36	        /// and on `prores_4444` a typed frame one pixel short. So no size of
    37	        /// the canvas's shape is refused for being odd; a typed size of any
    38	        /// other shape is judged as the even frame it becomes
    39	        /// (1279 × 720 on 1920 × 1080 is 1278 × 720 on `hevc_alpha`, and
    40	        /// refused).
    41	        ///
    42	        /// **Measured, not feared.** `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect` pads
    43	        /// the frame to the asked-for shape, and the padding path destroys
    44	        /// the alpha channel: a 320 × 180 transparent canvas written
    45	        /// `prores_4444` at 240 × 240 comes back with the PICTURE at alpha 0
    46	        /// and the letterbox BARS at alpha 255 — the answer inverted, not
    47	        /// merely lost. The same canvas at 160 × 90 or 640 × 360 is correct
    48	        /// at every pixel, so the fault is the padding and nothing else.
    49	        ///
    50	        /// It is refused rather than documented because the file would be
    51	        /// silently wrong in the one respect the row exists for, and this
    52	        /// codebase's rule for exactly that shape is `codecType(for:)`'s:
    53	        /// a refusal, never a fallback that puts a file on disk which is not
    54	        /// the one asked for. Nothing legitimate is blocked by accident —
    55	        /// every row of the Size popup is fitted to the document's own
    56	        /// aspect (`export_size.rs`), so only a hand-typed Custom size of
    57	        /// another shape can reach this (or a canvas, or a typed size, with

    62	        /// The user pressed Cancel. The sheet dismisses without an alert.
    63	        case cancelled

    97	            switch self {
    98	            case .noPlan:
    99	                return "The project could not be prepared for export."
   100	            case .emptyTimeline:
   101	                return "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."

   109	                    + "different shape, so the picture would be padded and the padding loses the "
   110	                    + "alpha channel. Export at \(width) × \(height), at one of the sizes in the "
   111	                    + "popup, or at any size with the same proportions."

   114	            case .failed(let message):

   116	            case .graphicsNotCompiled(let refused):

   118	                return "The export was not started: " + clauses.joined(separator: "; ")
   119	                    + ". Fix the module and export again."

   121	                return "The export was stopped at frame \(frame) of the graphic \"\(name)\": "
   122	                    + "\(message). No file was written."
   123	            case .graphicFailed(let name, nil, let message):

   125	                    + "\(message). No file was written."
   126	            case .rampAudioFailed(let clip, let message):
   127	                return "Clip \(clip)'s retimed audio could not be rendered: \(message)."
   128	            case .isolationFailed(let clip, let message):

   133	                    + "show the clip's loudness, then export again."
   134	            case .voiceFailed(let clip, let message):
   135	                return "Clip \(clip)'s voice effect could not be rendered: \(message)."
   136	            case .cutoutFailed(let clip, let message, let foreground):

   138	                    + "made: \(message)."
   139	            }
   140	        }
   141	    }

   143	    /// What a finished write becomes when the reason it failed is that this
   144	    /// Mac has no encoder for the row (spec §11 G-33 (e)): the preset's own
   145	    /// sentence, and no file.
   146	    ///
   147	    /// `ExportWriter.addVideo` cannot see it. Measured with an encoder
   148	    /// specification nothing satisfies, on `.hevcWithAlpha` and `.hevc`
   149	    /// alike: `canApply` is true, the input constructs, `canAdd` is true, and
   150	    /// `startWriting()` then fails with `AVFoundationErrorDomain` −11834
   151	    /// ("Cannot Encode"), leaving a 0-byte file at the destination. So it is
   152	    /// mapped here, where `startWriting` hears the pipeline: exactly that
   153	    /// domain and code become `.presetUnavailable` with the preset's name and
   154	    /// the file is removed, and every other result is returned as it came.
   155	    static func encoderOutcome(
   156	        _ result: Result<URL, any Error>, settings: ExportSettings, destination: URL
   157	    ) -> Result<URL, any Error> {
   158	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else { return result }
   159	        let reason = error as NSError
   160	        guard reason.domain == AVFoundationErrorDomain,
   161	            reason.code == AVError.Code.encoderNotFound.rawValue
   162	        else { return result }
   163	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
   164	        return .failure(ExportError.presetUnavailable(ExportWriter.presetName(settings)))
   165	    }
   166	}

     3	/// Writes the timeline to a file (spec §7.8), and renders one frame offline
     4	/// for the agent's verification hook.
     5	///
     6	/// The whole point of the design is that export and playback share exactly
     7	/// one description of the movie: the core's composition plan becomes the same
     8	/// `AVComposition` + `AVVideoComposition` (`CompositionBuilder`), and the same
     9	/// Metal compositor draws every frame from the same frame recipes. An export
    10	/// that disagreed with the preview would be a bug in one of those two, never
    11	/// in a second rendering path — because there is not one.
    12	///
    13	/// M1 was `AVAssetExportSession`: the core resolved a preset into concrete
    14	/// settings, this handed them over, and the sheet polled `progress`. M2's
    15	/// `AVAssetWriter` path (`ExporterWriter.swift`) has **replaced** it, and this
    16	/// file is otherwise unchanged — `export`, `cancel`, `finish`, `isRunning`,
    17	/// the progress timer, every `ExportError`, `renderFrame` and every
    18	/// settings helper (`ExporterSettings.swift` since phase 7) are what they
    19	/// were.
    20	///
    21	/// **Why the writer replaced the session outright rather than joining it.**
    22	/// The session path cannot express three things the sheet already promises:
    23	/// a chapter track (`AVAssetExportSession` writes none, so a `chapter: true`
    24	/// marker vanished on export), explicit bitrates (`ExportSettings` has
    25	/// carried `videoBitrate`/`audioBitrate` all along and a preset NAME can say
    26	/// nothing about them), and the resolved output size and frame rate — a
    27	/// preset scales to fit whatever it likes, so the sheet's "1920 × 1080 ·
    28	/// 25 fps" was a readout of numbers nothing downstream ever read. Keeping
    29	/// both paths would have made all three conditional: chapters when the
    30	/// project has them AND the codec took the writer, one quality rule here and
    31	/// another there, and two answers to "what did the file end up as". That is
    32	/// the same second-rendering-path this whole design exists to avoid, one
    33	/// layer down. The writer covers every preset the core offers — H.264, HEVC,
    34	/// ProRes and audio-only M4A — so there is no case left for the session to
    35	/// hold.
    36	///
    37	/// **The two formats AVFoundation cannot write** — animated GIF and APNG —
    38	/// are assembled frame by frame through ImageIO instead
    39	/// (`ExporterImageSequence.swift`), over `renderFrame`, which is why that one
    40	/// is static and takes no export state. Neither goes through AVFoundation at
    41	/// all, so neither is a branch of the writer path: they are a second
    42	/// pipeline, and `Exporter.pipeline` picks between the two on the core's
    43	/// `avf_preset`. Everything below the pick — the progress timer, `finish`,
    44	/// every `ExportError` — is shared, because the sheet cannot tell which one
    45	/// it got.
    46	///
    47	/// **Two passes, since phase 5.** An export that carries sound MEASURES its
    48	/// mix before it writes it (`Loudness.swift`), which is what lets the final
    49	/// line report "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS" for every export and what
    50	/// chooses the gain for one that asked to be normalised. That pass is
    51	/// **`ExporterLoudness.swift`** — this class's own extension, cut out when this
    52	/// file went past its size cap and otherwise unchanged — and its header carries
    53	/// the rest of the argument: what the pass costs, why it builds a composition
    54	/// of its own rather than sharing this one's mix, and why it reads float.
    55	///
    56	/// **Recipe options, since road map 2's phase 7.** `export` and `renderFrame`
    57	/// each take a `RecipeOptions` (spec §7.3) — what the caller wants of the
    58	/// PICTURE besides the timeline, today the burnt-in timecode. It is not an
    59	/// export override and cannot be made one: the core's override table ignores
    60	/// an unknown key on purpose, so an option sent that way would vanish and the
    61	/// export would report success on an unchanged file. Both entry points take
    62	/// it because they are two independent doors to the compositor — `export`
    63	/// publishes it on this export's `RecipeSource` key, which is what every
    64	/// frame `ExportWriter` reads back arrives through, while
    65	/// `ImageSequenceWriter` bypasses the writer entirely and renders each frame
    66	/// through `renderFrame`, on a key of its own. Both default to `.none`, so
    67	/// everything that does not ask writes what it wrote before.
    68	///
    69	/// **Settings → AVFoundation lives in `ExporterSettings.swift`** — the time

    73	/// file stood at exactly 600 lines. It is the same toll `ExporterLoudness.swift`

    86	    /// How often the sheet's bar is refreshed. Neither
    87	    /// `AVAssetExportSession` nor `AVAssetWriter` has a progress callback, so
    88	    /// the only way to draw a bar is to ask (spec §7.8); 0.1 s is smooth and
    89	    /// costs nothing.
    90	    static let progressInterval: TimeInterval = 0.1

    93	    /// opens asset tracks, which touches the disk. Same reason as
    94	    /// `Playback`'s, and a queue of its own so an export cannot make the next
    95	    /// preview rebuild wait behind it.
    96	    private let buildQueue = DispatchQueue(
    97	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export", qos: .userInitiated)
    98

   100	    /// ImageIO one, behind the three calls `Exporter` makes of either
   101	    /// (`ExportPipeline`).
   102	    private var writer: (any ExportPipeline)?
   103	    private var timer: Timer?
   104	    /// This export's own `RecipeSource` slot. NOT the document's: the document
   105	    /// republishes on every edit, and a frame already queued must not be
   106	    /// composed from a project the user changed halfway through the write.
   107	    private var recipeKey: Int?
   108	    /// Where this export writes — removed by `finish` when a graphic failed.
